content.content: deccy implements whole-operation undo and redo with markers over whole deccy operations: a marker names the operation's kind, the change it targeted and opaque entry ids, and the inverse is the one the kind names. A recording's inverse is a journal entry holding the before and after content of the paths it touched: undo applies the before side and returns the recorded diff to the working copy, redo applies the after side and removes it. A creation's or removal's inverse stays change-level. Undo records the inverse it applied; redo inverts that record.
content.rationale: One jj operation is finer than one deccy operation, so bare jj undo cannot undo a deccy operation; recording each operation's own record recovers operation granularity. A recording cannot be inverted from op-log entries alone: reverting the squash operation rewrites the working copy again and jj calls the next revert divergent, so a recording keeps its own before/after journal entry, written before the marker that names it. A creation and a removal are already whole changes, so their inverse stays change-level (abandon the created change, op-revert a removal's entries). The entries alone do not fix the inverse — D8a makes a creation's undo a removal of the created node and a recording's or removal's a restoration — so the inverse follows the operation's kind.
